accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England English Appendix 1 (Year 1 spelling: split digraphs a–e made, e–e these, i–e five, o–e home, u–e rule/June and cube), Letters and Sounds Phase 5 (split vowel digraphs as one grapheme for one phoneme) and CCSS RF.1.3c (final -e convention for long vowels). Every lab word was checked: cap/cape, kit/kite, hop/hope, cub/cube are real pairs; cake, bike, home are 3 phonemes, slide is 4; tap/tape, pin/pine, not/note, cut/cute contrast short and long vowels. The adult text notes the two u–e sounds and the have/give/come exceptions so nothing over-generalises.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Year 1 phonics errors: sounding the final e (challenge 'loud', m1), counting letters not phonemes (step 3 prediction, the 4-letters feedback in pickCount, challenge 'letters', p3, m8), reading the vowel short (step 5 prediction tape vs tap, m2), dropping the e in spelling to a different real word (step 4 kit/kite and hop/hope, m4), adjacent vowel teams mistaken for split digraphs (challenge 'side', m6), and tapping consonants as part of the digraph (step 2 feedback, challenge 'cons').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmagice is built around the split itself: an e tile dragged into an end slot that converts cap to cape, an arc drawn from the vowel over the consonant to the e, a sound count where letter count is the tempting wrong answer, and real-word swaps where the missing e changes meaning. flagvowel teaches adjacent vowel teams (ai, oi, oo) and flagdgraph consonant digraphs; neither has a split across a consonant. Gate similarity is under 30% to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule by acting: adding the e changes the word and the vowel message, dropping the e at the start is refused because it is not a word, tapping k in cake is refused because it makes its own sound, choosing 4 sounds for cake is refused with the letters-versus-sounds reason, and kit in I fly my kit is the word to fix. Each completion line states the rule just used.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: kit plus e keeps the short i (step 1, disproved by kite appearing), cake has 4 sounds one per letter (step 3, disproved by the 3-part count c, a–e, k), and tape is short like tap (step 5, disproved when the sort places it under says its name). The walkthrough reveal message confirms the right option after each task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Each wrong challenge choice maps to its own message: loud (e said aloud), swap (vowel letter changed rather than its sound), letters (counted letters), skip (missed consonant sounds), short (no e so vowel stays short), side (oa side by side is not split), cons (consonants picked), near (n and e chosen instead of u and e). Six questions rotate so a retry shows a different item.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK grade about 0 against the family target of 5, with short sentences and one new term (split digraph) explained as two letters that are apart. Lab prompts are under 12 words (Word 1 of 4: put the e on the end). Adult text is FK 8.9 against a 10 target and names the curriculum terms grapheme, phoneme, split digraph.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph teaches one idea (silent e makes the vowel say its name, the split team, the five digraphs, counting sounds). No banned phrases pass the content gate. Lab text is task or feedback only; each feedback line gives the specific reason for that word, e.g. A kit is a set of things. To fly it, you need kite.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: letter tiles are about 45 px on the phone and grow by 25% on desktop, the e tile is a separate large drag target, the sentence row in step 4 scales to fit 390 px, sort bins are half the width each, and every action also has a full-width button under the canvas. Nothing was clipped on any of the 6 steps.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate ran every step with Show me on desktop and iPhone and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme. Every drag or tap has a button equivalent (e at the end, letter buttons, 2 to 5 sounds, word buttons, both sort boxes), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each feedback message so a screen reader hears the result.
